modules.name: leakix
modules.live_check: Not called: key-only API and no team key; corporate decision SKIPPED licence (key-terms without key_plans.leakix=business), asserted live. Research 2026-11-25 recorded 401 'Invalid API key' for /host and /domain without a key (the real 401 fixtures). Every leakix.net web page (host, domain, search) redirects to /auth/login (checked 2026-11-26): references only, never a pivot-pack link.

core_requests: quota (P148 c3): a 'week' window in the P334 provider quota block (QuotaSpec has hour/day/month only); GreyNoise publishes 25-W keyless (~50/week keyed), so greynoise_community uses the interim Module.daily_quota = 3 and greynoise.json records the weekly limit under x_quota_window.

http (P274 c1): honour LeakIX's 429 header 'x-limited-for' (a Go duration, e.g. '344.24ms') like Retry-After (one wait/retry when <= 15 s), declared per provider; leakix reports RATE_LIMITED with the wait meanwhile.

sanitize (P274 c2): a sanitizer schema transform that keeps only the path of a URL field (e.g. keep_path_of: ['Leaks[].http.url']); keep lists cannot transform, so leakix keeps http.url and vetoes caching (cache_if) of answers whose kept URLs carry a query or fragment.

sanitize/http: null list values of a sensitive provider body ('Services': null) are dropped by apply_schema, so the module cannot tell {'Services': null, 'Leaks': null} from an unexpected object after sanitization; leakix declares error markers evaluated on the raw body before the allowlist. A keep-null option (or classification-only markers documented as running pre-sanitization) would make this explicit.

http: ScopedHttp.check()/_classify() re-classifies a response whose classification is None after the sensitive-body sanitizer replaced resp.content, so module error markers also run on the sanitized body (leakix's markers are written to never match the allowlisted forms). Classify once (resp._classified) instead of on 'classification is None'.

policy/engine (P148 c4): a per-run, per-provider note API (e.g. ctx.note_once(key, text)) so a hint such as GreyNoise's free-key hint is shown once per scan in the coverage line, not only in the first RATE_LIMITED reason and the live feed.

suppression (P148 c5-c7, P322): an engine-level registry of named suppression rules contributed by modules/packs (scope ip, cap severity, derived_from blocklist) - today the dampening is a correlation rule (g02_scanner_intel_dampening) that mutates findings in the correlation stage, like g10_sanction_dedup.
notes: All three proposals delivered as PASSIVE modules plus one correlation rule. Provider fragments created (hosts mapped to null in owners.json): greynoise (api.greynoise.io, viz.greynoise.io; tier trusted; key greynoise in the 'key' header; no quota block, weekly limit in x_quota_window), sans_isc (isc.sans.edu; tier trusted; http_profile user_agent 'contact' + Accept application/json - binding PROFILE_REQUIREMENTS - min_interval 2 s, one connection, no retries; source id sans_isc.api as in the WP07 licence_allow example), leakix (leakix.net; tier community; flags.sensitive true with the P274 allowlist as the source sanitizer keep list; quota scope key month 3000 published false; key leakix). Decisions to review: (1) P151 c3's '/api/asnum/{asn}' path is read by ISC as a count; the documented /api/asnum/{count}/{asn}?json (count 100) is used. (2) GreyNoise riot/benign and ISC research-scanner dampening is applied by correlation rule g02_scanner_intel_dampening through the named rules greynoise_riot, greynoise_benign_scanner, isc_research_scanner (no SUP- prefix so the findings stay CR27 evidence and CR27 keeps its own downgraded consensus): blocklist-derived findings (tags blocklisted/spam/scanner/malicious/suspicious/botnet) of other sources on that IP only are capped at LOW with a one-level label downgrade, c2/malware/phishing evidence untouched, nothing deleted, overrides never crossed, no dampening when GreyNoise itself reports malicious scanning. The modules also set the WP23 signals (finding tags known_good/benign_scanner, attribute scanner_classification, allowlisted) so CR27 downgrades consensus. (3) GreyNoise runs on analyst-typed seeds at depth 0 only (run_on 'seeds' + applies(): not pivots, not text-extracted values, not unconfirmed seeds). (4) LeakIX: full detail on seeds (depth 0) and org_profile own assets, counts only for pivoted third-party assets; on CDN/shared IPs (noise kinds cdn/cloud/hosting/saas) hits go to the hostname entity (Finding.entity) and hostless events stay unattributed counts; own DB/config exposures HIGH, other own leaks capped HIGH, non-own seeds capped MEDIUM; >90 days -> historical/POSSIBLE/'re-verify'. Because the provider is sensitive, the core sanitizer reduces bodies to the keep list before the module/raw/cache and also drops 'ip' fields and IP literals (second net); the module therefore attributes host lookups to the queried IP. LeakIX web pages need a login, so they are finding references (labelled) and not a pivot-pack/manual link. (5) P274 c7 merge gate is open: the success fixtures are synthetic (no team key); the recorded 401 fixtures are real - recorded in docs/backlog/p2-G02-3.md (also the ACTIVE 'status and size' confirmation variant of c5, which belongs to the late LIGHT/ACTIVE phase). (6) Acceptance routes added for ipv4 8.8.8.8 (greynoise_community: recorded 404; isc_dshield: recorded IP answer + research category) and replayed in the module tests.
